solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Choose dry red when touring with English MPs here

indicators.note: a group touring a place travels around it, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: to choose is to select
a red is a communist, colloquially a commie
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol: dry
E is the abbreviation for English, added on

explanation.surface: Politicians picking a dry red wine as they travel together in their parliamentary group.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is a standard crossword word for a communist, and TT (teetotal) for dry. 'MPs here' is the definition, describing the place by who meets in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A select committee is a small group of Members of Parliament appointed to scrutinise a particular area, so MPs sit there.

clue.text: Axe green areas of Paris to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: parcs is French for parks, green areas in Paris

explanation.surface: Someone proposing to cut the parks in Paris's northern districts.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe a plan or project is to cancel it, which is to scrap it: a verb synonym.

clue.text: Finally Plymouth Argyle – it's awfully far to go!

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the place name that follows it
something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out in a mangled order

blocks.note: the last letter of Plymouth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football fan grumbling about the long trip to watch Plymouth Argyle, a Devon football club at the far south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: H joins the anagram fodder with ARGYLE and IT; the 's (is) links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-year is the vast distance light travels in a year, so it is a very long way to go.

clue.text: Biting fish around lake

indicators.note: around means one word encloses the next on either side

blocks.note: a cod is a fish
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A fish taking a bite somewhere around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting wind is a bitterly cold one, so the adjectives are synonyms describing harsh weather.

clue.text: Pirate's vulgar song on the radio

indicators.note: what is on the radio is heard rather than seen, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: vulgar is coarse and a song is an air

explanation.surface: A pirate's rude shanty broadcast over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair is a privateer or pirate, especially of the Barbary coast: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Earned ceremony in the sea

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A burial or other ritual at sea that someone deserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something merited was deserved or earned, a past-tense verb synonym.

clue.text: Crucial to bring in worker

blocks.note: to bring goods in from abroad is to import them
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An employer saying it's vital to take on a new worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crucial is of great significance, which is what important means: an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Volunteers to lead a soldier up lots of freezing trees

indicators.note: to lead is to go in front, placing that word first
in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom, so the words run backwards

blocks.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
taken as written
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Reservists guiding a soldier up through a frozen forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiga is the vast subarctic coniferous forest of Siberia and Canada, a great many trees in a frozen climate.

clue.text: Earl leads girl to a flashy pad

indicators.note: the word that leads is placed in front of the next

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for Earl
Paulette is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A nobleman escorting a young woman to a fancy flat.
explanation.walkthrough: Pad looks like a home, as in a swanky bachelor pad; here it is the ornamental shoulder piece on a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is a decorative shoulder piece on a military coat, a showy padded strap.

clue.text: Controller loses to orderly

indicators.note: loses means some letters drop out of the word

blocks.note: a regulator is a controller
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A manager losing out to a hospital orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: Orderly looks like a hospital worker, but here it is an adjective meaning steady or methodical.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular and orderly both describe something arranged in an even, systematic pattern: adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Softly trace around a copy

indicators.note: around means one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: a relic is a trace left from the past
p, piano, is the musical direction for softly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gently tracing a picture to produce a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction of an object, so a copy: noun synonyms.

clue.text: Penny consumed spread

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for penny
consumed food means ate

explanation.surface: A cheap meal of something spread on bread, eaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté is a savoury paste of meat or fish eaten on toast, a food spread.

clue.text: Everyone's after torn pieces of cloth to make another one

indicators.note: after places that word behind the next one

blocks.note: tatters are torn scraps of cloth
everyone is all; the 's is 'is', joining the parts

explanation.surface: A patchwork maker turning old rags into a new piece of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another one' refers back to cloth in the wordplay: the answer is another type of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattersall is a woollen fabric with a check pattern, named after a London horse-market, so a further kind of cloth.

clue.text: Poet takes second to think of Nancy

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
penser is the French verb to think, as spoken in Nancy, a city in France

explanation.surface: A poet pausing a moment to think of a woman called Nancy.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a woman's name, but it is the French city, so the word for think is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Note from doctor, covering one priest in diocese

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around something, so the doctor's letters enclose what follows
in places the preceding group of letters inside the following word

blocks.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
the Roman numeral for one
Rev, Reverend, is a priest's title

explanation.surface: A note from the doctor about a priest in the diocese, perhaps a sick note.
explanation.walkthrough: Note looks like a written message from the doctor, but it is a musical note; there are two wrappings, one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A semibreve is a whole note in music, lasting four crotchet beats.

clue.text: Prudish girl entertains leader of Quaker's sect

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
to entertain guests is to take them in, so the name holds the letter

blocks.note: Sue is a girl's name
the first letter of Quaker
the Amish are a Protestant sect

explanation.surface: A girl hosting the head of a Quaker sect, who disapproves of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeamish person is easily shocked or offended, as is a prudish one, so the adjectives overlap in sense.

clue.text: Absolutely motionless at the games

blocks.note: dead means unmoving, as in dead still
a set is a group of games in tennis

explanation.surface: Players standing stock still at a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: Absolutely looks like part of the scene but is the definition, as in being dead set against something.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead set means utterly determined or completely, as in dead set on going, an intensifying phrase.

clue.text: Plain ties and green buckle

indicators.note: to buckle is to bend out of shape, so the letters lose their form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plain neckties and a green belt fastening, a dull outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain looks like an adjective about the ties, but it is a noun for open grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is the vast grassland plain of Tanzania famed for wildlife migration.

clue.text: Nob is replacing ends of rope and twine in posh tent

indicators.note: the ends of words are their final letters
replacing means one set of letters is swapped out for another

blocks.note: a marquee is a large grand tent
the final letters of rope and twine, the letters taken out
taken as written, the letters put in

explanation.surface: A tent at a smart event being repaired with new rope and twine.
explanation.walkthrough: A nob is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquis is a nobleman ranking above an earl, so a nob in the slang sense of a toff.

clue.text: Way to gag bird

blocks.note: St, street, is a way
to gag is to retch

explanation.surface: How to silence a bird, or how to choke one.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time; a stretch is the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretch is slang for a term in prison, as is bird, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Circle lake after a place to sleep

indicators.note: after places that word behind the next one

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Walking round a lake after finding somewhere to bed down.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive social group, the same sense as a circle of friends.

clue.text: Key I placed in bed for singer

indicators.note: placed in puts the preceding pieces inside the following word

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tucking a key into a bed, perhaps for a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Singer looks like a vocalist, but it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit is a small black-capped songbird, and singer is a crossword name for any songbird.

clue.text: Having dodgy locks is when mishaps occur

blocks.note: first meaning: a day when your hair looks unkempt
second meaning: any day when everything goes wrong

explanation.surface: A burglar with faulty locks is due some misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks suggests door fastenings, but they are tresses of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom literally describes a day of unruly hair and by extension a day of minor misfortunes.

clue.text: Miserable nurse at end of ward

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the final letter of ward
to nurse a child is to rear it

explanation.surface: An unhappy nurse stationed at the far end of a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read as 'nurse, at end of ward', putting the ward's last letter first.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning gloomy or dismal, close to miserable.

clue.text: Leaders of Kent's new orchestra tackle Ravel

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

blocks.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A new county orchestra in Kent attempting a piece by the composer Ravel.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel looks like the French composer of Boléro, but it is the verb meaning to tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to tangle threads together, which is what knotting them does: verb synonyms.

clue.text: It's not right to pack flip-flop

indicators.note: not here means that letter is excluded from the word

blocks.note: a throng is a crowd, a pack of people
R is the abbreviation for right, the letter dropped

explanation.surface: Someone saying it's wrong to put a flip-flop in the suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a simple sandal held on by a strap between the toes, the same footwear as a flip-flop.

clue.text: Yorkshire cricketer dropping a player? That's correct

indicators.note: dropping means letters are let go from the word

blocks.note: Fred Trueman was a famous Yorkshire and England fast bowler
a man is a player in a team, the letters dropped

explanation.surface: A selector confirming that a Yorkshire cricketer has dropped a teammate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true is accurate or right, so true and correct are adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Poet, left say, during robbery in Bow

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside it

blocks.note: a heist is a robbery; in Bow, East London, the Cockney accent drops the h
L is the abbreviation for left
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A poet who left during a robbery in an East London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in the East End of London, where Cockneys drop their h's.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist writes elegies, mournful poems, so is a kind of poet.

clue.text: Sub-standard rocket?

blocks.note: surface reading: below the expected quality
setter's reading: the standard missile fired by a submarine

explanation.walkthrough: Sub-standard reads as poor quality, but split as sub plus standard it means the regular weapon of a submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile, the stock armament of a submarine.

clue.text: Heather starting work of great importance

indicators.note: to work material is to knead and reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather beginning a job that matters a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth-shattering describes something so momentous it seems to shake the world, hence hugely significant.
